rules.statement: When a change adds, renames or removes a meter, instrument, attribute or attribute value, update the repository's metrics catalog document in the same change.
rules.why: The catalog is the reviewed contract that dashboards and alerts are built against, so it must never drift from what the code emits.
rules.check: Look for new or renamed Meter/Create* instrument names, tag keys or tag values in the diff with no matching edit to the metrics catalog doc (e.g. docs/metrics.md).

rules.statement: Never put a tenant, client, subject or other user identifier, or a network address, host or port, in a metric attribute; record those on traces or logs instead.
rules.why: Every distinct attribute value creates a new metric series, but on traces and logs cardinality costs nothing per series.
rules.check: Inspect TagList/KeyValuePair tags passed to counters and histograms for tenant ids, client ids, subjects, user names, IP addresses, URLs, server.address or server.port.

rules.statement: Give every metric attribute a bounded, server-defined set of values: map unregistered or unknown values to `_OTHER`, and never tag with free-form names or values a caller supplies.
rules.why: Unbounded or caller-controlled values blow up series cardinality and let callers create arbitrary series.
rules.check: Check that each tag value comes from a constant, registered name or enum, and that an unknown or caller-provided value (request parameters, free-form names) is replaced with `_OTHER` or a fixed constant.

rules.statement: Set `error.type` on a duration histogram or span only when the operation fails, and give it the exception's full type name or a fixed failure-reason constant.
rules.why: This keeps the attribute bounded and in line with the OpenTelemetry semantic conventions that dashboards rely on.
rules.check: Look for `error.type` added on success paths, or set to an exception message, ToString() or another free-form string instead of GetType().FullName or a reason constant.

rules.statement: In ASP.NET Core endpoint code, don't create a separate per-request duration instrument; add bounded tags to the built-in `http.server.request.duration` through `IHttpMetricsTagsFeature`.
rules.why: The hosting meter already measures each request, and a second instrument would duplicate that signal, which should have one owner.
rules.check: Flag new histograms or counters that time or count HTTP requests in endpoint or middleware code instead of using HttpContext.Features.Get<IHttpMetricsTagsFeature>().Tags.

rules.statement: In library packages, record telemetry only through `System.Diagnostics.Metrics` and `System.Diagnostics.ActivitySource`, and leave exporters and pipeline registration to the host.
rules.why: Instrumentation costs nothing until a listener subscribes, and the host decides how its signals are collected and exported.
rules.check: Look for OpenTelemetry SDK or exporter references, or MeterProvider/TracerProvider setup, in non-host library packages.

rules.statement: Give a package that traces its own work a single `ActivitySource` with the same name as its `Meter`, and expose both names as public constants.
rules.why: Hosts subscribe by name or prefix, and a matching source and meter name lets them add the package's metrics and traces together.
rules.check: Check that a new ActivitySource's name equals the package's Meter name, that there is only one per package, and that the names are public const fields rather than inline string literals.

rules.statement: When a span times the same operation as a histogram, give the span the histogram's attributes.
rules.why: Spans that mirror their histograms let a metric spike be traced to the matching spans by the same attribute values.
rules.check: Compare the tags set on a new Activity with those recorded on the matching histogram, and flag any that are missing or named differently.

rules.statement: Give durations the unit `s` and give counters a curly-brace annotation unit such as `{request}`, `{event}` or `{retry}`.
rules.why: This follows the OpenTelemetry unit conventions that the catalog and dashboards assume.
rules.check: Check the unit argument of CreateHistogram/CreateCounter calls: flag `ms`, missing units, or plain words without braces on counts.

rules.statement: Make an outbound HTTP client's retry policy retry only GET or HEAD requests without a body, and only after a transient failure: 408, 429, a 5xx status, a per-attempt timeout or a connection error.
rules.why: Only safe requests without a body can be sent again without risking duplicate side effects.
rules.check: Inspect retry predicates for POST/PUT requests, requests with content, or requests carrying single-use proofs such as DPoP being retried, or for retries on non-transient status codes.

rules.statement: When a host collects `System.Net.Http` metrics, add a view that keeps only bounded attributes and drops `server.address` and `server.port`.
rules.why: Those attributes name the hosts of client-registered or caller-supplied URIs, which makes them unbounded and identifying.
rules.check: Where AddMeter("System.Net.Http") is added, check that a view filters the tag keys down to bounded ones.
